seo.description: Plan Meknes: Bab Mansour, Place el-Hedim, Heri es-Souani, Moulay Ismail mausoleum, medina, Volubilis and Moulay Idriss Zerhoun. Hotels, food and a 3-day itinerary.
seo.og_title: Meknes Travel Guide | Imperial Gates & Roman Volubilis | MoroccoTripMap
seo.og_description: Imperial Meknes, Roman Volubilis and the holy town of Moulay Idriss — gates, granaries and a calmer medina than Fez.

hero_subtitle: Bab Mansour, Place el-Hedim, Heri es-Souani and the road to Roman Volubilis — the imperial city that still feels local.

overview.title: Meknes: Imperial Gates, Granaries and the Road to Volubilis
overview.p1: Meknes is the imperial city of Moulay Ismail: monumental gates, vast granaries and a medina that is easier to walk than Fez. Place el-Hedim and Bab Mansour set the scene; Heri es-Souani shows the scale of the sultan’s logistics. It is also the natural base for Volubilis and Moulay Idriss Zerhoun without the day-trip rush from farther cities.
overview.p2: Two full days cover the imperial core and the medina; a third day fits the Roman ruins and the holy hillside town. Stays cluster near the medina and Ville Nouvelle — practical if you arrive by train and want both history and calm evenings.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Imperial Meknes, then Volubilis and Moulay Idriss without rushing.
itinerary.day1: Day 1 — Place el-Hedim, Bab Mansour, medina & Dar Jamai
itinerary.day2: Day 2 — Mausoleum, Heri es-Souani & Medersa Bou Inania

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start on Place el-Hedim while the square is still quiet. Face Bab Mansour, walk the gate details, then enter the medina lanes for a first orientation and coffee.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Continue through the medina souks toward Dar Jamai Museum. Keep the pace slow — Meknes rewards looking up at woodwork and courtyards more than ticking boxes.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Return to Place el-Hedim for sunset light on the gate. Dinner near the square or in a medina riad restaurant.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visit the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail early (check opening rules and dress). Then head to Heri es-Souani for the granaries and stables while the light is still soft.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Medersa Bou Inania for tilework and quiet courtyards, then free time in Ville Nouvelle or a second medina loop for crafts and olives.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Rooftop or simple grill near the medina. Rest early if tomorrow is Volubilis.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Drive or grand taxi to Volubilis. Walk the forum, triumphal arch and mosaics before the heat builds.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Continue to Moulay Idriss Zerhoun. Climb to a viewpoint, respect the sacred character of the town, then return to Meknes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last evening in Meknes — Place el-Hedim once more or a calm dinner before a train to Fès or Rabat.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Meknes
places.subtitle: Gates, square, granaries, museum, Roman ruins and the holy town nearby.

bab.title: Bab Mansour
bab.desc: The ceremonial gate facing Place el-Hedim — the postcard of imperial Meknes.

hedim.title: Place el-Hedim
hedim.desc: Main square for orientation, evening light and the view of Bab Mansour.

ismail.title: Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail
ismail.desc: Imperial resting place with controlled access and refined craft.

heri.title: Heri es-Souani
heri.desc: Vast stables and storehouses that show the logistics of Moulay Ismail’s state.

medina.title: Meknes Medina
medina.desc: Souks and lanes calmer than Fez, still full of daily life.

jamai.title: Dar Jamai Museum
jamai.desc: Palace museum of craft and domestic life on the edge of the medina.

volubilis.title: Volubilis
volubilis.desc: UNESCO Roman city in the olive hills — mosaics, forum and arch.

idriss.title: Moulay Idriss Zerhoun
idriss.desc: White hillside town above the ruins — sacred and photogenic.

medersa.title: Medersa Bou Inania
medersa.desc: Merinid medersa with tile, wood and a quiet courtyard in Meknes.

directory.title: Hotels & Riads in Meknes
directory.subtitle: Medina riads near Place el-Hedim and practical stays in Ville Nouvelle.

h1.name: Riad d’Or
h1.desc: Courtyard calm a short walk from Place el-Hedim.

h2.name: Riad Meknes
h2.desc: Traditional house restored for travellers who want the medina first.

h3.name: Hotel Transatlantique
h3.desc: Classic option with space and easy taxi access to the imperial sites.

h4.name: Ryad Bahia
h4.desc: Intimate riad useful as a base before Volubilis.

h5.name: Hotel Rif
h5.desc: Practical for train arrivals and longer stays.

h6.name: Maison d’Hôtes Zitouna
h6.desc: Simple guesthouse atmosphere near the souks.

eat.title: Where to Eat in Meknes
eat.subtitle: Square terraces, medina grills and reliable Ville Nouvelle tables — not Marrakech copies.

placehedim.title: Terraces on Place el-Hedim
placehedim.desc: Mint tea and simple meals with Bab Mansour in view — best at golden hour when the gate lights up.

medina_grill.title: Medina grills & olive stalls
medina_grill.desc: Skewers, bread and olives where locals eat. Follow busy tables rather than empty tourist boards.

riad_restaurant.title: Riad courtyard restaurants
riad_restaurant.desc: Set menus in restored houses a few minutes from the square — book for a quiet dinner.

ville_nouvelle.title: Ville Nouvelle cafés & brasseries
ville_nouvelle.desc: Coffee, pastries and easier seating after a day on your feet near the train station side of town.

rooftop.title: Rooftop viewpoints
rooftop.desc: A few rooftops near the walls for sunset over the imperial city — ask your riad for the current best table.

local_tagine.title: Tagine & couscous houses
local_tagine.desc: Slow-cooked standards. Ask for the day’s pot rather than a fixed tourist menu only.

transport.title: Getting around without wasting time
transport.desc: The medina and Place el-Hedim are walkable. Use petits taxis for Heri es-Souani and the mausoleum if heat is high. For Volubilis and Moulay Idriss, hire a grand taxi for a half-day or join a small tour so you are not stuck waiting for returns. The train station sits in Ville Nouvelle — budget a short taxi to the medina on arrival.

water.title: Heat, water and timing
water.desc: Summer on the plateau is harsh at midday. Do Heri es-Souani and Volubilis in the morning, carry water, and use the medina’s shade for afternoons. Spring and autumn give the most comfortable light on Bab Mansour and the Roman stones.

bargain.title: Shopping and expectations
bargain.desc: Souks are calmer than Fez. Polite bargaining is normal for crafts, spices and olives. Fixed-price museum tickets and official sites leave little room for negotiation — keep energy for the medina stalls instead.

cash.title: Cash, dress and access rules
cash.desc: ATMs in Ville Nouvelle and near the main square. Smaller cafés prefer cash. Dress modestly for the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail and in Moulay Idriss Zerhoun; some areas may be restricted to non-Muslims — follow posted signs and local guidance without argument.

daytrips.title: Day Trips from Meknes
daytrips.subtitle: Roman ruins next door, the holy town, and easy links to Fès or the Middle Atlas.

fes.title: Fès
fes.desc: One hour by train — the great medina when you want intensity after Meknes’s calmer streets.

rabat.title: Rabat
rabat.desc: Capital day by train: Kasbah of the Udayas and Hassan Tower without changing hotels.

volubilis_combo.title: Volubilis & Moulay Idriss
volubilis_combo.desc: The classic half-day loop: mosaics in the olive hills, then the white town above.

ifrane.title: Ifrane & Middle Atlas
ifrane.desc: Cedar forest and cooler air when you need a break from imperial stone.

azrou.title: Azrou
azrou.desc: Market town and cedar country — monkeys and mountain light on a full day.

q1.question: How many days in Meknes?
q1.answer: Two days for the imperial sites and medina; three if you include Volubilis and Moulay Idriss Zerhoun without rushing.

q2.question: Is Meknes worth visiting compared to Fès?
q2.answer: Yes if you want monumental gates and a less overwhelming medina, plus the easiest base for Volubilis. Many travellers do both.

q3.question: How do I reach Volubilis?
q3.answer: Grand taxi, private driver or organised half-day tour from Meknes. Public transport alone is awkward for a comfortable visit.

q4.question: Is the medina safe to walk?
q4.answer: Yes during the day with normal city awareness. Keep valuables close and use taxis at night between Ville Nouvelle and the medina if you prefer.
